patients.summary: Administrative assistant with hypertension who joined in 2018, then developed major depression (sertraline), recurrent right trigeminal neuralgia (carbamazepine) and a toxic right thyroid nodule treated with I-131. After her last practice visit in October 2025 she was diagnosed with left inflammatory breast carcinoma, HER2-positive, and the chart ends during post-mastectomy radiation.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
46F joining us after her old office stopped taking her plan. Works as an administrative assistant at an insurance agency office in town, sits most of the day.

HTN for several years per her, on lisinopril 10 daily, no side effects, home cuff readings in the 120s. No other chronic problems. No surgeries. NKDA.

FHx: mom with high blood pressure, maternal aunt had breast cancer at 54, sister treated for depression.
SHx: smokes roughly a pack a week, has for about 20 years. Says she really wants to stop and has tried cutting down on her own. Drinks once or twice a month at most. Single, lives alone.

ROS negative.

Exam: well appearing. BP and vitals as charted. Thyroid not enlarged, no nodules felt. Heart RRR without murmur, lungs clear. Breasts symmetric without masses, no axillary nodes. Abdomen soft. No edema. Skin clear.

A/P
1. Essential HTN, controlled on lisinopril 10. Continue. BMP today.
2. Tobacco: about 3 pack-years. Talked through quit options including patch or medication; she wants to try a quit date first, will let me know. Not in range for lung screening.
3. Health maintenance: CBC, CMP, fasting lipids, one-time hep C and HIV screen today. Signed release for the old office so we get her last mammogram and Pap. Mammogram due in the fall. Colon screening discussed, she wants to wait a bit.
PHQ-2 negative.
RTC 6 months, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Result Note
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Labs reviewed. Blood counts, kidney and liver panel, cholesterol all normal. Hep C and HIV negative. Portal message sent.

events.reason: Low mood, tired all the time

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Booked this herself after the holidays. For about six months she has felt flat and heavy, hard to get going, nothing feels worth the effort. Sleeping as much as 12 hours on weekends and still tired. Up about 15 lb since summer per our scale and hers. Cannot point to anything that changed: same job, same apartment, nothing happened. Still getting to work but describes it as going through the motions. No SI, no plan, no prior episodes. Sister has been treated for depression. No alcohol increase.

Exam: flat affect, good eye contact, linear. Thyroid normal size, no nodule. Heart and lungs normal. No edema.

PHQ-9 17. GAD-7 6.

A/P
Depressed mood with hypersomnia and weight gain, 6 months, moderately severe by PHQ-9. Checking TSH and fasting glucose today to rule out the obvious medical causes. She would like to see psychiatry before starting anything; referral placed, marked soon. Crisis line info given and she knows to call me same day if mood dips further.
HTN: BP fine today, continue lisinopril.
Smoking: still at a pack a week; not the right moment for a quit attempt, will revisit.

documents.title: Result Note
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: TSH normal. Fasting glucose 98. Nothing medical showing up to explain the fatigue. Psychiatry intake is Jan 25. Message sent to pt.

conditions.label: Major depressive disorder, single episode, moderate

procedures.procedure: Psychiatric diagnostic evaluation with medical services

documents.title: Outpatient Psychiatry Consultation
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
OUTSIDE PSYCHIATRY GROUP - CONSULTATION LETTER
Visit 01/25/2019. Thank you for referring Ms. Marsh, 47.

Presenting problem: half a year of sadness, low energy and poor drive that has steadily deepened. She now sleeps up to twelve hours a day and has put on roughly fifteen pounds. She denies any precipitating event or change at home or work.

Medical: hypertension, controlled on lisinopril 10 mg daily. No drug allergies.
Family: sister with major depression; mother hypertension; maternal aunt breast cancer at 54.
Substances: smokes, which she minimized at first and then said she has wanted to give up for years, about a pack weekly over two decades. Alcohol a drink or two a month. No drugs.

Vitals within normal limits per our intake. Physical screening exam unremarkable. Your TSH (normal) and fasting glucose of 98 reviewed.

Mental status: casually dressed, psychomotor slowing, mood 'empty', affect constricted, thought process goal directed, no SI or HI, no psychotic features, insight fair.

Impression: Major depressive disorder, single episode, moderate, with atypical-leaning features (hypersomnia, weight gain).

Plan: sertraline 50 mg daily. Referral to individual therapy; she has the list. Follow-up here in 6 weeks. Safety plan reviewed.

Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Sertraline question
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, the psychiatrist started me on sertraline about two weeks ago. My stomach has been a little off in the mornings. Is that normal or should I stop? I don't want to bother her office if it's nothing.

documents.title: RE: Sertraline question
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Very common in the first couple of weeks and it usually fades. Taking it with breakfast helps. Don't stop it. If it isn't better in another week, or anything else comes up, let her office or me know.

documents.title: Psychiatry Follow-up
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body: Follow-up 03/08/2019. Ms. Marsh reports some lift in energy, getting up earlier, but mood still low most days. Early nausea resolved. Has had two therapy sessions. No SI. Partial response at 6 weeks; increasing sertraline to 100 mg daily. Return in 2 to 3 months. Meds: sertraline 100 mg daily, lisinopril 10 mg daily. NKDA.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up. Mood noticeably better since the sertraline went to 100; sleeping 8 to 9 hours now, back to walking at lunch. PHQ-9 down to 9. Seeing a therapist every other week. Weight holding, not going up.
BP good on lisinopril. BMP today.
Exam: brighter affect. Heart regular, lungs clear.
A/P: MDD improving on sertraline 100, psychiatry following. HTN controlled. Still smoking, no change; she wants mood steady first. Recheck in the fall.

documents.title: Result Note
documents.author: RN
documents.body: BMP normal per PCP, pt notified via portal.

events.reason: Sharp pain right side of face

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Texted Friday asking to come in. About three weeks of jolts of pain on the right side of her face, like a zap, seconds long, several a day. Brushing her teeth sets it off reliably so she has been brushing the right side gently or not at all. Nothing between attacks. No rash, no dental work, no jaw clicking, no headache, no vision change.
Exam: no facial asymmetry, no rash. Teeth and gums look normal, no tender tooth on percussion. TMJ nontender. Cranial nerves II-XII intact, facial sensation normal to light touch, corneal reflex not tested. Strength and gait normal.
A/P: Brief triggered unilateral facial pain, sounds like trigeminal neuralgia. Neurology referral to confirm and start treatment; she prefers to let neuro choose the drug. Tylenol in the meantime though it likely won't touch it.
Mood: doing well, psychiatry visit Friday.

documents.title: Psychiatry Follow-up and Transfer of Care
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
Follow-up 06/07/2019. Ms. Marsh describes her mood as close to her usual self for about a month. Energy and sleep normalized; working and socializing again. Mentions new facial pain, already referred to neurology. No SI.
Assessment: MDD, single episode, responding well to sertraline 100 mg.
Plan: continue sertraline 100 mg daily for at least a year of remission before any taper discussion. She may continue therapy as she wishes. Returning medication management to primary care; happy to see her again if symptoms recur.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily

documents.title: Neurology Consultation
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE NEUROLOGY - CONSULTATION
Date of visit: 07/15/2019

Ms. Marsh is a 47-year-old woman with treated hypertension and a depressive episode earlier this year, now on sertraline, seen for two months of right facial pain. She characterizes each attack as an electric jolt or stab on the right side of the face, lasting under a minute and recurring many times through the day. Toothbrushing is the most consistent trigger. She has had no change in vision, no fever and no other neurologic complaint.

Medications: lisinopril 10 mg daily, sertraline 100 mg daily. NKDA.
Family history: mother hypertension; sister depression; maternal aunt breast cancer.
Social: smokes about one pack weekly for twenty years and hopes to quit; rare alcohol; administrative assistant.

Examination: alert, fluent. Cranial nerves intact including facial sensation in all three divisions and masseter strength. Motor, sensory, reflexes, coordination and gait normal.

Impression: classic right trigeminal neuralgia.

Plan: carbamazepine 200 mg twice daily. Reviewed dizziness, rash and low sodium as things to report. Please check CBC and sodium in about a month. Phone follow-up in 2 months.

documents.title: Result Note
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: One month on carbamazepine. Sodium normal, white count and platelets normal. Copy faxed to neurology. Pt says the face pain stopped within about a week of starting it.

documents.title: Neurology Telephone Follow-up
documents.author: neurology
documents.body: Phone visit 09/24/2019. Pain-free for about seven weeks on carbamazepine 200 mg twice daily, a little drowsy in the evenings. Labs from PCP reviewed, normal. As remissions are common, we agreed on a two-week taper to off: 200 mg once daily for a week, then 100 mg nightly for a week, then stop. She will call if attacks return; we can restart at the prior dose.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Influenza Vaccine
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Came over on lunch. Quad flu IM right deltoid. Tolerated. Physical booked for December.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual. Mood good, PHQ-9 4, taking sertraline 100 every morning, no longer in therapy. Face pain came back toward the end of October after neuro tapered her off in September; fewer attacks than spring but same character, mostly with brushing. She already called neurology and has a January appointment; doesn't want to restart on her own. Tylenol does little.
Still smoking a pack a week. Tried a quit date in August, lasted four days. Offered patch and Chantix again, wants to try again on her own after the holidays.

Exam: well. BP and vitals as charted. HEENT normal. Thyroid without enlargement or nodules. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Breasts without masses, nipple changes or axillary adenopathy. Abdomen soft, no organomegaly. Extremities without edema. Neuro nonfocal.

A/P
1. HTN controlled on lisinopril 10.
2. MDD in remission on sertraline 100. Continue at least through mid-2020.
3. Trigeminal neuralgia, recurrent, off carbamazepine. Neuro in January.
4. Tobacco, counseled 5 min.
5. HM: mammogram order placed. Lipids and BMP today. Colonoscopy discussed again, she will think about it after 50.

documents.title: Result Note
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Lipids normal, BMP normal. Sent to portal.

reports.text: Digital screening mammography with tomosynthesis, CC and MLO views of each breast. Comparison 11/2018 and 11/2017. Heterogeneously dense breast tissue. No new mass, asymmetry, distortion or suspicious calcifications.  Skin normal.
reports.conclusion: BI-RADS 1, negative. Return to annual screening.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily

documents.title: Neurology Follow-up
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE NEUROLOGY - FOLLOW-UP
Date of visit: 01/22/2020

48-year-old woman with hypertension and a depressive episode last year, in remission on sertraline, back with the same right facial pain we treated in July 2019. It returned roughly three months ago, a few weeks after the carbamazepine taper. Attacks are abrupt stabs over the right cheek and upper lip, under a minute each, several per day. A light touch to the cheek or brushing her teeth can set one off. She has no headache with them, no visual aura, no light sensitivity, and no tearing, redness or nasal symptoms. No facial injury, infection or recent dental procedure.

Meds: lisinopril 10 mg, sertraline 100 mg. NKDA.

Vitals normal. Exam: cranial nerves normal, no facial weakness, facial sensation preserved in all divisions between attacks. Remainder of neurologic exam normal.

Impression: recurrent right trigeminal neuralgia, V2 distribution.

Plan: restart carbamazepine 200 mg twice daily, the dose that worked before. CBC and sodium through PCP in a month. Follow-up in 4 months; if she stays pain-free we can try another taper.

documents.title: Result Note
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: CBC and sodium normal on carbamazepine. Faxed to neuro.

documents.title: Neurology Video Follow-up
documents.author: neurology
documents.body: Video visit 05/19/2020 (clinic converted to virtual). No attacks since early March. Some daytime fog on carbamazepine that she would like to be rid of. February labs normal. We will taper again over two weeks and stop. If pain recurs she should call us. Routine follow-up in 6 months.

documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE NEUROLOGY - FOLLOW-UP
Date of visit: 01/18/2021

49-year-old with hypertension and major depression in remission, seen here for this facial pain in 2019 and 2020. Pain has been back for about six months: sudden severe sharp pains on the right, now over the cheek and down into the lower jaw, lasting from a few seconds up to two minutes. Chewing and brushing her teeth set it off, and at times just a breeze across her face. She has never had a rash or skin lesion there.

Medications: lisinopril 10 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg daily, sertraline 100 mg daily. NKDA.
Social: still smoking about a pack per week, wants to quit; social alcohol; administrative assistant.

Exam: face symmetric, no skin lesions, no palpable masses. Light touch over the right cheek provokes a typical jab of pain. Remainder of neurologic exam unremarkable.

Impression: trigeminal neuralgia, right V2 and V3, third recurrence after medication withdrawal.

Plan: restart carbamazepine 200 mg twice daily and this time continue as maintenance rather than tapering. Sodium and CBC through her PCP, especially with the thiazide on board. Follow-up in 6 months.

documents.body: Seen 07/13/2021. Trigeminal neuralgia well controlled on carbamazepine 200 mg twice daily, only rare brief twinges with chewing. Tolerating; mild evening tiredness. Exam unchanged and normal. Plan: continue current dose indefinitely. Please keep checking sodium and CBC periodically with her routine labs. Return here as needed or yearly.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual. Back in the office three days a week. No new concerns. BP log at goal. TN quiet on carbamazepine. Mood good, PHQ-9 3; she asked whether she could come off sertraline at some point, we agreed to keep it through the winter and revisit.
Smoking: same, a pack a week, she brought up quitting herself. Discussed patch plus short-acting NRT; she wants to set a date around New Year's.
Exam: BP and vitals as charted. HEENT normal. Neck supple, thyroid not palpable. Heart regular without murmur. Lungs clear. Breasts without mass, skin change or adenopathy. Abdomen soft. No edema. Mood euthymic.
A/P
1. HTN controlled, continue lisinopril 10 and HCTZ 12.5.
2. TN on carbamazepine; CMP and CBC today for sodium and counts.
3. MDD in remission.
4. Tobacco, counseled.
5. HM: flu vaccine given. Lipids today. Turns 50 in January: colonoscopy and shingles vaccine next visit. Mammogram up to date. Pap due 2022. COVID booster at the pharmacy.

documents.title: Colonoscopy Report
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GI GROUP - COLONOSCOPY
Date: 05/17/2022. Indication: average-risk screening, first colonoscopy, age 50.
Sedation: monitored anesthesia care with propofol.
Prep: good (BBPS 8).
The scope was passed without difficulty to the cecum, confirmed by landmarks and photographed. Withdrawal time 9 minutes. Mucosa normal throughout the colon and rectum. No polyps, no diverticula. Retroflexion in the rectum normal.
Impression: normal screening colonoscopy.
Recommendation: repeat screening in 10 years.
Allergies: NKDA.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
About two months of feeling her heart pounding, sometimes racing at rest, always too warm while everyone else is cold, and eating more but the scale keeps dropping, down about 7 lb from our October weight. No chest pain, no fainting, no diarrhea, periods unchanged. No new meds or supplements. No neck pain.
Exam: HR 104 regular, BP as charted. Thyroid: possible fullness on the right, hard to be sure. No eye findings. Heart tachycardic, no murmur. Lungs clear.
A/P: Symptoms fit hyperthyroidism. TSH, BMP and CBC today. If TSH is low I'll refer to endocrinology right away. Return precautions for chest pain or fainting. Smoking same; told her tobacco and an overactive thyroid both strain the heart.

documents.title: Your thyroid test
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your TSH came back very low (under 0.01), which means the thyroid is making too much hormone. That fits how you've been feeling. I've placed an urgent endocrinology referral; their office will call you. Your other labs were normal. If your heart races and doesn't settle, or you get chest pain, call me right away.

documents.title: RE: Your thyroid test
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thank you, honestly relieved there's a reason. They called already, first opening is Jan 20 and they want me to do a scan a few days before.

documents.title: Thyroid Uptake and Scan
documents.author: nuclear medicine
documents.body:
OUTSIDE NUCLEAR MEDICINE
Exam: I-123 thyroid uptake and scan, 01/17/2023 (uptake measured at 4 and 24 hours).
Indication: suppressed TSH, possible right thyroid nodule.
Findings: focal intense radiotracer accumulation corresponds to a nodule in the right lobe. The remaining right lobe and the entire left lobe show suppressed uptake. No additional foci.
Impression: hyperfunctioning right thyroid nodule with suppression of the remaining gland, consistent with a toxic adenoma.

documents.title: Endocrinology Consultation
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE ENDOCRINOLOGY - NEW CONSULT
Date of visit: 01/20/2023

Ms. Marsh, 51, with hypertension, a past episode of major depression and recurrent trigeminal neuralgia, comes in with three months of a pounding heartbeat, heat intolerance and a ten-pound weight loss even though she is hungrier than usual. Bowel habits and menses have not changed.

Medications: lisinopril 10 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg daily, carbamazepine 200 mg twice daily, sertraline 100 mg daily. NKDA.
Family history: mother hypertension; sister depression; maternal aunt breast cancer at 54. No known thyroid disease.
Social: smoker, about a pack per week for 20 years, wants to quit. Social alcohol. Administrative assistant.

Exam: BP 145/90, HR 102. Fine tremor of the outstretched hands. A non-tender nodule is palpable in the right thyroid lobe. No proptosis, lid lag or pretibial skin change.

Labs today: TSH <0.01 mIU/L (0.4-4.0), free T4 3.0 ng/dL (0.9-1.7), free T3 8.0 pg/mL (2.3-4.2).
Uptake scan 01/17/2023: hot right nodule with suppression of the rest of the gland.

Assessment: toxic single thyroid nodule (toxic adenoma) with overt hyperthyroidism.

Plan: methimazole 10 mg daily to bring levels down, atenolol 25 mg daily for heart rate and tremor. Discussed definitive options; she prefers radioactive iodine over surgery. Will schedule I-131 in about 6 weeks, holding methimazole for several days beforehand. CBC and liver tests are not needed routinely but call for sore throat with fever or yellowing. Follow-up 6 to 8 weeks after treatment.

documents.title: Thyroid plan
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Saw endo. They think it's one nodule on the right that's overactive. I'm on methimazole and atenolol now and doing radioactive iodine in March. Do I keep taking my blood pressure pills too?

documents.title: RE: Thyroid plan
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Yes, keep the lisinopril and HCTZ. The atenolol is for heart rate and shakiness and may lower your BP a bit more, so if you feel lightheaded or home readings are under 100 on top, let me know. I got their letter and updated your list.

documents.title: I-131 Therapy
documents.author: nuclear medicine
documents.body:
OUTSIDE NUCLEAR MEDICINE - RADIOIODINE THERAPY
Date: 03/08/2023. Indication: toxic adenoma, right thyroid lobe.
Methimazole held since 03/03/2023.
Administered 15 mCi I-131 sodium iodide orally. Tolerated without event. Radiation safety instructions reviewed in writing.
Methimazole is not to be resumed unless endocrinology advises. Continue atenolol. Follow-up with endocrinology in 8 weeks with TSH and free T4.

documents.title: Endocrinology Follow-up
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body: Seen 05/10/2023, about 9 weeks after 15 mCi I-131 for a right toxic adenoma. Palpitations, heat intolerance and tremor gone; appetite back to normal, some weight regained. TSH 1.1, free T4 1.1: euthyroid, off methimazole. Stopping atenolol today. No thyroid hormone needed. Hypothyroidism can still develop later, so please check TSH yearly, or sooner for fatigue, cold intolerance or weight gain. No routine return here needed.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
OUTSIDE EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT - PHYSICIAN RECORD
Arrival 01/19/2026 18:40.

CC: left breast pain and swelling x 2 months.

HPI: 54F with HTN, depression, trigeminal neuralgia and a toxic thyroid nodule treated in the past, here because her left breast has been getting larger and more painful over about eight weeks and in the past couple of weeks has turned red and hot. She thought it was an infection and waited for it to pass. No fever. No nipple discharge. No injury.

PMH: hypertension (on hydrochlorothiazide and lisinopril), major depressive disorder, trigeminal neuralgia, toxic thyroid nodule s/p radioiodine.
Meds: lisinopril 10 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg daily, carbamazepine 200 mg BID, sertraline 100 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
FHx: no breast cancer in first-degree relatives.
SHx: smokes about a pack per week for 20 years and wants to quit; drinks socially 1-2 per month; administrative assistant.

Exam: afebrile, vitals stable as recorded. Left breast diffusely enlarged compared with the right, erythematous and edematous, with peau d'orange skin. Warm. No discrete palpable mass. Left nipple retracted. Firm palpable left axillary lymph nodes. Right breast and axilla normal. Heart and lungs normal.

Labs: CBC within normal limits. ESR 52 (elevated).

MDM: picture is concerning for inflammatory breast cancer rather than mastitis or abscess given duration, absence of fever, peau d'orange, nipple retraction and adenopathy. Discussed with on-call breast surgery. No antibiotics. Urgent outpatient diagnostic breast imaging arranged for 01/21 and breast surgery/oncology evaluation. Patient understands and agrees. Asked to notify her PCP.

Disposition: discharged home 23:10, stable.

documents.title: Went to the ER last night
documents.author: patient
documents.body: I should have called you weeks ago. My left breast has been swollen and sore since late November and then got red, I figured an infection. Went to the ER last night. They said it might be inflammatory breast cancer and I have imaging tomorrow. I'm scared. I had a normal mammogram in September, how can this happen?

documents.title: RE: Went to the ER last night
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Melissa, I'm so glad you went in, and I'm sorry you're dealing with this. This kind of breast cancer, if that's what it is, often grows quickly and doesn't form a lump, so it can appear after a normal mammogram. Nothing you did caused it. Tomorrow's imaging and a biopsy are the right next steps, and I'll make sure we get every report. Please call or text me today if you'd like to talk it through, I'm around all day. Keep taking all your usual medicines.

documents.title: RE: RE: Went to the ER last night
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thank you. I'll call at lunch.

events.reason: Diagnostic breast imaging, left breast swelling

reports.text: Left diagnostic mammogram with tomosynthesis; right breast CC and MLO for comparison. Compared with screening study of 09/2025. Left breast: diffuse skin thickening and trabecular thickening with overall increased density relative to prior and to the right breast. No discrete mass, suspicious calcification or focal distortion. Enlarged dense left axillary lymph nodes are partially included. Right breast unchanged and negative.
reports.conclusion: Findings of the left breast highly suggestive of inflammatory breast carcinoma in this clinical setting. BI-RADS 5. Tissue sampling recommended.

reports.text: Targeted ultrasound of the left breast and left axilla. Diffuse skin thickening and subcutaneous edema throughout the left breast. No discrete solid mass identified. Left axilla: several enlarged lymph nodes with thickened cortex and effaced fatty hilum, the largest 2.2 cm.
reports.conclusion: Skin thickening and edema without discrete mass; abnormal left axillary lymph nodes, largest 2.2 cm. BI-RADS 5. Ultrasound-guided biopsy of breast and axillary node recommended; MRI for extent.

documents.title: Breast Imaging Reports Received

documents.body: Diagnostic mammogram and ultrasound reports from the outside breast center, dated 01/21/2026, received by fax and filed. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: MRI Breasts With and Without Contrast
documents.author: radiology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE BREAST CENTER - MRI BILATERAL BREASTS WITH AND WITHOUT CONTRAST
Date: 01/23/2026. Indication: clinical concern for inflammatory carcinoma of the left breast; BI-RADS 5 mammogram and ultrasound.
Technique: standard bilateral breast protocol with dynamic post-contrast imaging.
Findings: Left breast: extensive non-mass enhancement occupying much of the breast, spanning about 8.5 cm, with diffuse skin thickening and enhancement indicating skin involvement. No discrete enhancing mass. Pectoralis muscle without abnormal enhancement. Left axilla: multiple enlarged lymph nodes with abnormal morphology, suspicious for metastasis. Right breast: no suspicious enhancement. Right axilla normal.
Impression: extensive left breast non-mass enhancement with skin involvement and suspicious left axillary lymphadenopathy, consistent with inflammatory breast carcinoma pending pathology. Right breast negative. BI-RADS 5.

events.reason: Breast, axillary node and skin biopsies

reports.text:
Specimens: (A) left breast, ultrasound-guided core needle biopsy x4; (B) left axillary lymph node, ultrasound-guided core biopsy x3; (C) left breast skin, punch biopsy.
A: invasive ductal carcinoma, Nottingham grade 3. Estrogen receptor 0%, progesterone receptor 0%. HER2 by immunohistochemistry 3+ (positive).
B: metastatic carcinoma consistent with breast primary.
C: dermis with tumor emboli within lymphatic channels; epidermis intact.
reports.conclusion: Left breast invasive ductal carcinoma, grade 3, ER-negative, PR-negative, HER2-positive (IHC 3+), with dermal lymphatic tumor emboli and a positive left axillary lymph node. Findings support inflammatory breast carcinoma.

documents.title: Breast Biopsy Procedure Note
documents.author: breast surgery
documents.body:
OUTSIDE BREAST SURGERY - PROCEDURE NOTE
Date: 01/26/2026. Procedures: ultrasound-guided 14-gauge core biopsy of the left breast (4 cores) and of the largest left axillary node (3 cores), with clip placement in the node; 4 mm punch biopsy of left breast skin, lower outer quadrant. Local anesthesia. No complications. Hemostasis with pressure; punch site closed with one suture.
Pathology attached (resulted 01/29). Medical oncology consult already scheduled 01/28; results discussed with patient by phone today. Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Medical Oncology Consultation
documents.author: medical oncology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE CANCER CENTER - MEDICAL ONCOLOGY NEW PATIENT CONSULTATION
Date of visit: 01/28/2026
Referred from the ED via breast surgery. PCP copied.

History: 54-year-old woman with hypertension, major depressive disorder in remission, trigeminal neuralgia and a toxic thyroid nodule treated with I-131 in 2023, who noticed left breast swelling and soreness about two months ago, followed by redness and warmth. Screening mammogram 09/2025 was negative. No fever, discharge or trauma. Seen in the ED 01/19.

Meds: lisinopril 10 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg daily, carbamazepine 200 mg twice daily, sertraline 100 mg daily. NKDA.
Family history: maternal aunt with breast cancer at 54; mother hypertension; sister depression.
Social: smoker, roughly one pack weekly for 20 years, motivated to quit; social alcohol; administrative assistant, lives alone.

Exam: ECOG 0. Left breast enlarged, erythematous and edematous over more than a third of the skin, peau d'orange, nipple retracted, no discrete mass. Firm mobile left axillary nodes. No supraclavicular nodes. Right breast normal. Lungs clear. Liver not enlarged.

Data: diagnostic mammogram and US 01/21, BI-RADS 5, largest axillary node 2.2 cm. MRI 01/23: non-mass enhancement about 8.5 cm with skin involvement and left axillary adenopathy. Biopsies 01/26: invasive ductal carcinoma grade 3, ER 0%, PR 0%, HER2 3+; axillary node positive; dermal lymphatic emboli. CEA 7.8 ng/mL and CA 15-3 64 U/mL today, both elevated. Chemistries otherwise normal.

Assessment: inflammatory breast carcinoma, left, HER2-positive, hormone receptor-negative, clinical stage IIIB (cT4d cN1), distant staging pending.

Plan:
1. PET/CT for staging.
2. Baseline echocardiogram before trastuzumab.
3. Port placement.
4. Neoadjuvant docetaxel, carboplatin, trastuzumab and pertuzumab (TCHP) every 3 weeks for 6 cycles, then modified radical mastectomy and post-mastectomy radiation; HER2-directed therapy to complete one year.
5. Antiemetics and supportive medications will come from our office. She may continue sertraline and carbamazepine; we will watch counts closely.
6. Smoking cessation strongly encouraged; referred to our tobacco program.
7. Social work and nurse navigator introduced.

documents.title: PET/CT Skull Base to Mid-thigh
documents.author: radiology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE CANCER CENTER - FDG PET/CT
Date: 02/02/2026. Indication: staging of newly diagnosed left inflammatory breast carcinoma.
Findings: Hypermetabolic diffuse left breast parenchyma and thickened overlying skin. Hypermetabolic left axillary lymph nodes, levels I and II. No hypermetabolic internal mammary, supraclavicular or mediastinal nodes. Lungs without suspicious nodule. Liver, adrenal glands and spleen without suspicious uptake. No suspicious osseous lesion. Thyroid without focal uptake.
Impression: hypermetabolic left breast and left axillary nodal disease. No evidence of distant metastatic disease.

reports.text: Complete 2D, M-mode and Doppler study. Left ventricle normal in size and wall thickness with normal systolic function; LVEF 62% by biplane method. Normal regional wall motion. Normal diastolic filling. Right ventricle normal size and function. Atria normal. Valves structurally normal without significant regurgitation or stenosis. No pericardial effusion. IVC normal with normal respiratory variation.

OUTSIDE SURGERY - OPERATIVE NOTE
Date: 02/06/2026. Procedure: placement of right internal jugular single-lumen chest port under ultrasound and fluoroscopic guidance.
Indication: neoadjuvant chemotherapy for left breast cancer.
Anesthesia: local with moderate sedation. Port pocket in the right upper chest. Catheter tip at the cavoatrial junction on fluoroscopy. Flushes and draws well. Estimated blood loss minimal. No complications. Accessed and ready for use. Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Oncology Treatment Note - Cycle 1
documents.author: medical oncology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE CANCER CENTER - INFUSION VISIT
02/09/2026. Cycle 1 day 1 of TCHP (docetaxel, carboplatin, trastuzumab, pertuzumab), every 21 days x 6. PET/CT without distant disease: stage IIIB confirmed. Echo LVEF 62%. Port in place. Labs adequate for treatment. Premedication and antiemetics per protocol. Breast unchanged from consult. Plan: cycle 2 on 03/02. Medications per our list; continue home lisinopril, HCTZ, carbamazepine, sertraline. Copy to PCP.

documents.title: Chemo started
documents.author: patient
documents.body: First round done. Tired and my stomach is unhappy but the nurses are great. Oncology said keep the sertraline and carbamazepine. Is it okay with you to stay on the blood pressure pills, my BP was a bit low at infusion?

documents.title: RE: Chemo started
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good to hear from you. Your oncology team checks your pressure every visit, so follow what they say on the blood pressure pills; if you feel dizzy standing or your home readings run under 100, hold the HCTZ and let both of us know. I'm reading every note they send. Text me anytime.

documents.title: Oncology Treatment Note - Cycle 3
documents.author: medical oncology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE CANCER CENTER - INFUSION VISIT
03/23/2026, cycle 3 day 1 TCHP. After two cycles: fatigue for about a week after each, alopecia, loose stools managed with the supportive plan. No fever or neutropenic events. Exam: left breast erythema and edema have resolved, peau d'orange no longer seen, breast softer; axillary nodes no longer palpable. Labs acceptable. Proceed. Clinical response encouraging. Cycle 4 on 04/13.

reports.text: Limited 2D and Doppler study for LV function surveillance on trastuzumab. Left ventricle normal in size with normal systolic function; LVEF 58% by biplane method, compared with 62% on 02/03/2026. No regional wall motion abnormality. Valves without significant dysfunction. No pericardial effusion.

documents.title: Oncology Treatment Note - Cycle 5
documents.author: medical oncology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE CANCER CENTER - INFUSION VISIT
05/04/2026, cycle 5 day 1 TCHP. Tolerating with the same fatigue and loose stools. Breast exam: no erythema, edema or skin change; no palpable axillary nodes. Echo today LVEF 58%, within normal and not a meaningful decline; continue HER2 therapy. Proceed with cycle 5. Final cycle 05/26, then surgical referral for modified radical mastectomy about 4 to 6 weeks later.

documents.title: Oncology Treatment Note - Cycle 6
documents.author: medical oncology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE CANCER CENTER - INFUSION VISIT
05/26/2026 (moved a day for the holiday). Cycle 6 of 6 TCHP, completing neoadjuvant chemotherapy. Exam: complete clinical response in the breast and axilla. Plan: left modified radical mastectomy 06/29 with breast surgery; trastuzumab and pertuzumab to continue every 3 weeks after surgery to finish a year of HER2-directed therapy; radiation oncology referral placed for post-mastectomy radiation.

documents.title: Surgical Discharge Summary
documents.author: breast surgery
documents.body:
OUTSIDE HOSPITAL - DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 06/29/2026, discharged 06/30/2026.
Diagnosis: left inflammatory breast carcinoma, HER2-positive, after neoadjuvant TCHP.
Procedure 06/29/2026: left modified radical mastectomy (total mastectomy with level I and II axillary dissection), no immediate reconstruction as is standard for inflammatory carcinoma. Two closed suction drains. Estimated blood loss under 100 mL. No complications.
Course: overnight observation, pain controlled with oral medication, ambulating, tolerating diet. Drains with serosanguinous output. Home medications resumed: lisinopril 10 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg, carbamazepine 200 mg twice daily, sertraline 100 mg daily. Short course of oral pain medication per surgery.
Follow-up: breast surgery clinic in 1 week for pathology and drain check. Allergies: NKDA.

reports.text:
Specimen: left modified radical mastectomy with axillary contents, after neoadjuvant chemotherapy.
Breast: tumor bed with fibrosis and treatment effect; no residual invasive carcinoma and no residual ductal carcinoma in situ. Skin and nipple: no carcinoma; no dermal lymphatic tumor emboli. Margins: not applicable, no residual tumor.
Lymph nodes: 0 of 14 involved; biopsy-clipped node identified with treatment effect, no residual tumor.
reports.conclusion: No residual invasive or in situ carcinoma in breast or 14 lymph nodes (ypT0 ypN0): pathologic complete response.

documents.title: Breast Surgery Post-op Note
documents.author: breast surgery
documents.body:
OUTSIDE BREAST SURGERY - POSTOPERATIVE VISIT
07/06/2026, one week after left modified radical mastectomy. Healing well, incision clean and dry, flaps viable, no seroma. Both drains removed today. Arm range of motion exercises reviewed. Pathology reviewed with her: pathologic complete response, ypT0 ypN0. She was tearful with relief. Next: radiation oncology 07/14 and continued trastuzumab/pertuzumab with medical oncology.

documents.title: Radiation Oncology Consultation
documents.author: radiation oncology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE CANCER CENTER - RADIATION ONCOLOGY CONSULTATION
Date: 07/14/2026.
54-year-old woman with left inflammatory breast carcinoma, cT4d cN1 M0, ER/PR-negative, HER2-positive, treated with 6 cycles of neoadjuvant TCHP and left modified radical mastectomy on 06/29/2026 with pathologic complete response (ypT0 ypN0, 0/14 nodes). Continuing trastuzumab and pertuzumab.
Meds: lisinopril, hydrochlorothiazide, carbamazepine, sertraline; HER2 therapy per medical oncology. NKDA.
Exam: left mastectomy incision healed, no erythema; shoulder range of motion near full. No palpable adenopathy.
Recommendation: post-mastectomy radiation to the left chest wall and regional lymph nodes, 50 Gy in 25 fractions, regardless of pathologic response given inflammatory presentation. Risks reviewed including skin reaction, fatigue, lymphedema, and small risks to lung and heart. Consent signed. CT simulation 07/22, start planned 08/03. HER2 therapy can continue concurrently.

documents.title: Good news and a refill
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Wanted you to hear it from me: the surgery pathology showed no cancer left. Radiation starts August 3, every weekday for five weeks. Could you send refills for sertraline and carbamazepine? Pharmacy says no refills left.

documents.title: RE: Good news and a refill
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: That is wonderful news, Melissa. I saw the pathology report come in and was hoping you'd write. Sertraline 100 and carbamazepine 200 twice daily are sent, 90 days each. If you want help with quitting, I can send patches whenever you say. Thinking of you through radiation.

documents.title: Radiation Oncology Treatment Start
documents.author: radiation oncology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE CANCER CENTER - RADIATION ON-TREATMENT NOTE
08/03/2026: fraction 1 of 25 to the left chest wall and regional nodes, 2 Gy per fraction, total planned 50 Gy. Setup verified with imaging. Tolerated without issue. Skin care instructions given. Weekly on-treatment visits. Anticipated completion early September. Trastuzumab and pertuzumab continuing every 3 weeks with medical oncology, next 08/10.
